Availability varies by model and AWS Region. Check the model's detail page for Reserved Tier support and the Provisioned Throughput support table for availability. After you do so, the support team will reach out and offer you the option of also increasing the other two quotas.\\n\\n **Note:**\\n\\n Due to overwhelming demand, priority will be given to customers who generate traffic that consumes their existing quota allocation. Approval depends on whether your existing usage justifies the increase, so include recent usage information from CloudWatch or the Service Quotas console with your request\",\"url\":\"https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/quotas-mantle.html\"},{\"rank_order\":4,\"title\":\"How do I troubleshoot the \\\"ThrottlingException\\\" error when I use Amazon Bedrock on-demand resources?\",\"context\":\"### Request a quota increase\\n\\nNew AWS accounts might have lower initial quotas than the default quotas. Specific models have non-adjustable fixed quotas. If your workload traffic exceeds your account's on-demand quotas, then contact [AWS Support](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/awssupport/latest/user/case-management.html#creating-a-support-case) or your account manager to [request a quota increase](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/quotas-increase.html). AWS might adjust default quotas based on usage patterns or service requirements.\\n\\nInclude the following information in your request:\\n\\n* The name of the quota to increase\\n* Your current quota value and the quota value that you require\\n* The model ID\\n* The Region for the quota increase\\n* A brief explanation of your use case\\n* Your projected usage, including steady and peak tokens and requests per minute, and average input and output tokens per request\",\"url\":\"https://repost.aws/knowledge-center/bedrock-throttling-error\"},{\"rank_order\":5,\"title\":\"Request an increase for Amazon Bedrock quotas\",\"context\":\"# Request an increase for Amazon Bedrock quotas\\n\\nQuota increase requests in Amazon Bedrock differ depending on which endpoint you use. To request an increase, see the section that applies to your endpoint:\\n\\n* For `bedrock-runtime` quotas, see Requesting a quota increase.\\n* For `bedrock-mantle` quotas, see Requesting a quota increase\",\"url\":\"https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/quotas-increase.html\"}]}}"}]}], "label": "Search AWS docs for Bedrock quota increase guidance"}

{"id": "62d4a9f9-ab82-4882-b967-2312de9a5eac", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"text": "Here's how to raise the quota, based on the current Bedrock documentation.

## Requesting the increase

1. **Find the quota that's throttling you.** Open the Service Quotas console for Amazon Bedrock in the Region where you're calling. Look for the on-demand InvokeModel quotas for your model: requests per minute and tokens per minute. If you use a cross-Region inference profile, the relevant quota is "Cross-Region InvokeModel tokens per minute for <model>".
2. **Check the Adjustable column.**
   - **Yes:** request the increase directly in Service Quotas. For a tokens-per-minute quota, request it on the **Cross-Region InvokeModel tokens per minute** entry. AWS Support will then offer to raise the on-demand tokens-per-minute and Cross-Model Max Tokens Per Day quotas together with it.
   - **No:** the quota is fixed for that model. Open an AWS Support case or contact your account manager.
3. **Put these details in the request:**
   - The quota name, and the current and requested values.
   - The model ID and the Region.
   - A short description of your use case.
   - Your steady and peak requests and tokens per minute, and your average input and output tokens per request.

## Things that affect approval

- **Usage counts.** AWS prioritizes customers who are actually consuming their existing quota. Your request may be denied if you aren't, so include recent CloudWatch usage data.
- **Model lifecycle.** Increases aren't granted for Legacy or Deprecated models. Check the model's status first and consider moving to its successor.
- **New accounts.** New accounts often start with lower quotas.
- **`bedrock-mantle` endpoint.** If you use this endpoint, the Service Quotas console doesn't process increases. Submit them through the AWS Support limit increase form, choosing Amazon Bedrock as the service.

## While you wait

- Add retries with exponential backoff and jitter. AWS recommends this for every 429 response.
- For sustained, predictable throughput, look at **Provisioned Throughput** or **Reserved Tier**. Availability depends on the model and Region. Reserved Tier is arranged through your AWS account team.
- Spread load across Regions with cross-Region inference profiles. These also have higher throughput limits.

I can check your current Bedrock quotas and recent throttling metrics in this account if you tell me the model ID and Region.", "type": "text"}], "created_at": null}
